## 2026-11-27 - ECurves: a drop marker while dragging from the browsers
Asked: when a model is dragged from the model browser into ECurves, show exactly where it will be placed before the mouse button is let go. Done: while a model, ECurve primitive or library shape is dragged over the view, a marker shows where it lands. It is a ring with a filled disc, ticks and a stem lying on the surface under the pointer (the nearest solid, else the ground), kept the same size on screen. For a model, a box shows its bounds as it will stand there. The model is read on a worker the first time it is dragged over the view, and the drop then uses that read, so it is added at once with no wait. The marker hides when the pointer leaves the view or the drag ends; reads that were not dropped are freed, never waited for on the main thread. shape_tools.drop_hit gives the point and its normal; drop_point uses it, so the marker and the drop always agree. Files: scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd (_drop_marker, _make_drop_marker, _box_lines, _drop_bounds, _read_done, _drop_marker_end, _take_drop_read; _can_drop_shape, _drop_shape, _process), scripts/editor/mesh/shape_tools.gd (drop_hit), tests/test_curve_modeling.gd (test_drop_marker_shows_where).

## 2026-11-27 - ECurves: Auto join (solids meeting along an edge made one)
Asked: when converting to ECurves or baking an object with several solids, solids that share an edge (near
the same place, near the same shape) are joined into one solid with one of the shared edges removed ("auto
join"), also a separate action; no gaps, holes, topology or shading distortions; materials, bone weights and
bone associations kept.
Done:
- scripts/editor/mesh/auto_join.gd (new; pure functions, run on a worker):
  - find_pairs: an edge of each solid, both open borders of their meshes, compared by 48 even points (both ways' farthest distance within the merge distance or 3% of the shorter edge, lengths within 12%); only solids of one group (the same bone, both skinned or not).
  - join: the meshes as one (quads from paired triangles), each pair welded: each side's points matched along the kept edge (by place along it); a point one side lacks is put on it by a loop cut through its quads from the seam (each quad split in two, carried across till an open side or a triangle - quads stay quads; new inside points bent onto the surface by their ends' normals); both sides read again after every cut (a cut can come round onto the seam). Then the points are made one, the dropped edge removed, triangles two solids both had in one place (touching face to face) removed as a union would, points no one uses dropped.
  - Materials: each triangle's from its solid; stored as anchors (a point inside each material's stretch) + seams, so tri_materials finds them again after edits/settles; split_by makes a surface per material with the same normals (no shading seam).
- curve_tools.gd: auto_join(ps, quiet, must) gathers the solids and starts the worker; _join_step puts the result in (the others' edges moved into the kept solid's place, its spec, metas) as one undo step (_join_set); _joined_weights joins the old solids' weight sources (bones renumbered to the kept skin by name, missing binds added); _mats_step/_mats_apply split a joined solid's single-surface mesh into its materials each time it's made (labels cached by its triangles' hash; read back from the saved surfaces on load).
- Triggers: after a conversion (the converted solids; the batch store waits for it), after Bake (groups with the baked solid), the menu (view right-click ECurves page; the overview's solid and collection menus).
- Numbers on the user's character: 91 solids -> 72; 28 shared edges welded (Chest Glow + Chest Joint 5, shins/forearms/head 2 each...); every seam side has two faces after; no new non-manifold sides; quads kept (e.g. 839 of 842); a join 43-160 ms on a worker; detection 0.35 s on a worker. Undo/redo checked.
- Tests: test_curve_modeling.test_auto_join_after_converting (two tube halves, two materials: one solid, 3 edges, nothing open at the seam, >=90% quads, two surfaces each in its half, normals equal across the weld, undo/redo).
- Docs: data/docs/editor.md (Auto join under Bake).
Files: scripts/editor/mesh/auto_join.gd (new), scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd, data/docs/editor.md.

## 2026-11-27 - ECurves: Merge by distance
Asked: a function to merge vertices by distance.
Done: curve_tools.merge_by_distance (Alt+M; right-click menu with vertices, a solid or nothing picked): vertices within the merge distance made one - next to each other on one edge: one dissolved; on different edges: moved together to their middle (the solids follow). Scope: the picked vertices, else the picked edges', else the picked solid's, else all. One undo step; points already in one place aren't counted again.
Tests: test_curve_modeling.test_merge_by_distance. Docs: data/docs/editor.md (picked vertices section).
Files: scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd, tests/test_curve_modeling.gd, data/docs/editor.md.

## 2026-11-27 - ECurves browsers and overview: item tooltips with the item itself turning; categories; sharp previews
Asked: browser items show only their own tooltips, with a much bigger preview and their info - not the
browser's tooltip (that only over its tab); the same for the overview's entries, with no clash with Godot's
own tooltips there; slower turning of the hover previews in the lists and in the tooltips; previews never
pixelated; categories in the browsers (models: NPCs, creatures, ships, stations...).
Done:
- PinTips (scripts/ui/pin_tips.gd): over an ItemList, the hovered item's own tooltip (never the list's; Godot's own turned off for that item), nothing between items; over a tree, nothing between rows. A tooltip can show the item: "tip_view" (Callable -> a Mesh / Node3D) - TipView, or "tip_pic" (a picture, never shown bigger than its own pixels). screen_scale() - the interface's scale on the screen.
- scripts/ui/tip_view.gd (new): the item in a small lit world of its own, turning once in 5 s, drawn at the screen's own pixels (a 280 px box is 560 px on a 4K screen at scale 2) - no turntable strips kept in memory.
- MeshEditor._tip_pics: views for the models (read on a worker the first time, the last 6 kept, waited for on exit), primitives (the basic shape in the editor's look), materials (a ball), the overview's solids (as they are now) and collections. The overview's row and button tooltips are taken for PinTips on first hover (tree_tip) so Godot's never shows beside it.
- The lists' own tooltips moved to their tabs (meta "tip_on_tab"; test_tooltips accepts it); model items' tooltips titled (name, path, character / edited notes); overview rows titled with the solid's / collection's name.
- Slower: TurntableHover 18 -> 5 frames a second (a turn ~5 s); tooltip views turn once in 5 s.
- Sharper: the model list's thumbnails rendered at 160 px (shown 72 px = 144 screen px at 4K; MeshThumbs size per instance, its disk files apart); materials stay 128 (shown 56).
- Model categories (MODEL_CATS): All, NPCs, Creatures, Ships, Stations, Buildings, Props, Yours - buttons with counts under the search, empty ones greyed (the game's ships, stations and creatures are procedural - not model files - so those are 0 for now).
- Docs: data/docs/editor.md (the ECurves editor section).
Files: scripts/ui/pin_tips.gd, scripts/ui/tip_view.gd (new), scripts/editor/mesh_editor.gd, scripts/editor/mesh/mesh_thumbs.gd, scripts/editor/turntable_hover.gd, scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd, tests/test_tooltips.gd, data/docs/editor.md.
